Subject: Re: Initial: Importex tax certificate and bank info for PO activation

Hi Anna — thanks for the certificate and bank summary. Quick checklist from our side so we can map the correct pay-to entity and assign a PO: 

1) Legal entity verification: full legal name exactly as it should appear on the PO (and any branch names).
2) VAT / tax ID copy (you provided — thanks). Please also confirm whether the VAT ID is active for B2B domestic supplies vs. cross-border exports.
3) Which entity should be issued the PO? (Importex Ltd. — Poland) or a German fiscal rep? PO assignment affects tax handling and withholding.
4) Confirm remittance currency and preferred bank wiring details in IBAN + SWIFT format (we need them in the PO activation step).
5) If you intend to invoice us from a non-EU account, confirm if you will include VAT on invoices or if reverse-charge will apply (we may need a signed EU tax residency declaration).

If you can complete the short PO intake form in the Drive folder (link below) and return the fiscal representative letter if applicable, we should be able to generate the PO within 48–72 business hours.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1ImportexOnboard

Best,
Marissa Cole
Manager, Strategic Procurement
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Anna — looping in AP ops as well so we can get the entity mapping right before PO creation. Marissa: I attached the PO entity matrix we use internally — it lists the legal name fields we need and the remittance mappings for multi-entity vendors.

Quick asks for Importex to fill in the matrix (attached):
- Official pay-to legal name exactly as it should appear on the PO
- Registered VAT/Tax ID (confirmed) and country of registration
- Do you invoice from Importex Ltd. (PL) or the German fiscal rep (if so, we need their fiscal rep letter and tax registration)?
- Preferred invoice currency and bank account (IBAN + SWIFT)
- Any payment terms exceptions (Net30 default; if you require Net45 or different sign-off, note here)

We try to avoid creating a PO against a fiscal representative unless absolutely required for tax/regulatory reasons — it complicates remittance and VAT reclaim.

Attachment: PO-entity_matrix_Importex.xlsx (XLSX, 85KB)

Ben Carter

Subject: Re: Initial: Importex tax certificate and bank info for PO activation

Hi all — a couple of tax points to close this out cleanly: 

• If Importex Ltd. (PL) will be the invoicing entity to Redwood (B2B), and you are VAT-registered in Poland, then typically we apply reverse-charge (no VAT charged by vendor) for cross-border services. We will need a copy of your active VAT certificate (received) and a short vendor declaration confirming the nature of supply (services vs. goods).

• If you invoice from the German fiscal representative entity, we need the fiscal rep appointment letter AND confirmation that the rep is the legal invoicing entity. That will change whether VAT is applied and which entity appears on the PO.

• For PO activation: please confirm the exact pay-to name and supply the bank details as IBAN + BIC/SWIFT (we cannot activate POs with partial bank lines). If you prefer payments to a non-EU bank, note that bank-level currency conversions may trigger additional review and KYC.

• DocuSign: I created a short EU tax residency declaration template for Importex to sign so our AP team has records in case of audit. Link below — please sign after you populate the PO matrix.
  https://www.docusign.com/teams/xyz/Importex-PO

Once we receive the completed PO-entity matrix and the (if applicable) fiscal rep letter, AP will set up the vendor, and we can issue the PO. Expected timeline: 2 business days after complete docs.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Tax & AP Liaison
Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
